conventions: Svelte 5 runes only — no `class:name`, use `:class={...}`. Bind via `$props()`. State via `$state()`, derived via `$derived()` / `$derived.by()`.
Rune-based exports: `export const foo: Set<X> = $state(new Set())` — sets are reactive state.
Frontend test pattern: 1131+ existing vitest assertions; use existing `createNetwork` / `createBuffer` helpers in ircStore.svelte.test.ts (around line 200-300).
Synchronous state-machine setters in ircStore.svelte.ts; mutations are direct because runes auto-react.
Buffer-level fields added over time are namespaced by W-plan ID in comments (W1-T06, W7-T01, W1-T08). Preserve these markers when editing nearby code.
Markdown plan artifacts: plan.yaml + context_envelope.json + plan-summary.md committed to docs/plan/<plan-id>/
Reuse-before-rewrite principle: helper extraction preferred over inline body duplication (see AGENTS.md reuse_notes).
Frontend /local proxy endpoints are reachable via VITE_SIGNOZ_URL etc. — no env tweaks needed for the IRC rejoin work.

gotchas.text: setActiveBuffer auto-creates phantoms with isJoined=false. Sync handler at line 1385-1391 phantoms differently from real buffers — the joinInFlight=true guard at 1388 prevents sync from adopting a phantom into isJoined=true. The slash/URL-nav paths use maybeAutoJoinChannel which already handles this. The Wave 1 helper must apply the same quartet (joinInFlight=true + pendingIsJoined=true) for phantoms too.

resetPendingState at WS reconnect does NOT clear activeJoinList (line 440-443). This is by design — activeJoinList is a short-term buffersToDelete guard that must survive the WS-resume window so freshly-joined buffers aren't reaped before the sync confirms them. InitiateRejoin calling recordJoin is therefore correct: it survives WS resume via the design.

Both .join-inflight-chip (BufferHeader line 174) and .join-error-chip (line 179) render in an {:else if} chain — failure response REPLACES the optimistic joining state, not transiently shows both. Therefore 'no flicker on 473' is structurally guaranteed — no animation suppression code needed.

ChannelContextMenu renders the Rejoin item only when isActive === false (line 243-244). isActive derives from buf.isJoined !== false AND net.connected. So on a disconnected network, the menu shows Rejoin, but the engine's connected state means clicking it triggers a JOIN that won't reach the IRC server — currently BufferHeader.rejoin's reconnectNetwork branch is the right pattern.
IRCCloud visual vocabulary is opacity/italic for joining (no spinner). Using opacity transitions keeps it fast and avoids competing with the .join-inflight-chip spinning dot already in BufferHeader.

Task T2 (prePopulateOwnNick at click time): the dedup uses stripPrefix so a 353 follow-up with `@me` does NOT create a duplicate. Existing 353 in-place promotion at line 1696-1701 reads the existing entry, sets nick='@me' (with prefix char), and updates prefix='@' and category.

WS-reconnect race: clicking Rejoin on a disconnected network fires reconnectNetwork (BufferHeader allowReconnect=true) AND recordJoin in one frame. After WS resume, resetPendingState clears pendingJoins + joinInFlight + pendingIsJoined + pendingConfirmations but PRESERVES activeJoinList. A subsequent sync that arrives before the engine's JOIN-echo has propagated can show isJoined=false for one round-trip. W3-T04 test #10 documents this flicker window. The user's helpers do NOT currently mark the buffer in a separate reconnectQueue (would survive resetPendingState) — out of scope.

prior_decisions.decision: The sync-clobber architecture (2-of-2 confirming sync guard + joinInFlight short-circuit) is correct. Do not redesign.
rationale: Existing test coverage at ircStore.svelte.test.ts:860-1348 pins the architecture in place.
W7-T01 plan shipped the pendingIsJoined + pendingConfirmations quartet specifically to handle WS-round-trip race.
Marginal change is to make every rejoin entry point conform; invasive redesign risks regressions.

prior_decisions.decision: Extract initiateRejoin rather than inline the fix in each of the 4 entry points.
rationale: Allows a single test suite to pin the invariants.
Prevents re-occurrence if a future rejoin entry point is added.
Matches the user's 'reuse, don't rewrite' guidance — maybeAutoJoinChannel is the canonical pre-existing pattern.

prior_decisions.decision: sidebar gets .buffer-item--joining modifier rather than a separate component.
rationale: Lightest-touch change preserving existing visual vocabulary (.unread / .highlight).
Avoids new component lifecycle wiring for a single visual flag.
User acceptance explicitly calls out 'within 50ms' — class binding is the lowest-latency reactivity primitive in Svelte 5.

prior_decisions.decision: prePopulateOwnNick at click time uses stripPrefix dedup — same rule as 353 handler.
rationale: The 353 in-place promotion at line 1696 depends on stripped-nick dedup. Pre-population must not break that.
Test at ircStore.svelte.test.ts:1378-1398 'does not duplicate own nick when 353 arrives after JOIN' confirms the rule.

prior_decisions.decision: Sidebar mirror modifier .buffer-item--joining applies to ALL FOUR channel buffer-item sites (150 Pinned, 251 Active, 293 Inactive, 364 Archived) and explicitly excludes line 324 (DM/conversation).
rationale: All four channel sections can contain a buffer that has just been clicked for rejoin (Pinned channels are reachable via the pinned index). Conversations (DMs) never have joinInFlight because /join does not target a user.
Style vocabulary: matches existing .buffer-item.unread / .buffer-item.highlight modifier classes (italic + reduced opacity).

prior_decisions.decision: Drop PART-before-JOIN from /cycle /hop /rejoin (slashCommands.ts:205-206). Wire only a single JOIN via initiateRejoin.
rationale: PART-before-JOIN clobbers isJoined=true mid-flow and breaks the optimistic Joining chip — the core UX bug this plan is fixing.
IRCCloud's /cycle semantics is 'just rejoin' — PART is implicit when the user explicitly chooses to rejoin from the channel view.
Behavior change is logged in docs/CHANGELOG.md under the next release.
